title: Hermes Source Spec v0.1
description: Declarative contract for a job-source adapter. Describes WHAT to do (HTTP, pagination, extraction paths, safety policy, completeness rules). Contains NO executable code. The runtime evaluates the spec; the source provider only contributes the JSON. v0.1 supports offset pagination only — page_number and cursor are intentionally NOT advertised; they will land in v0.2 when a real source needs them.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract that this spec targets.

url.description: Absolute URL of the catalog endpoint. May contain {{stable_id}}-style placeholders only when paging.inject.target = 'url_path'.

query.description: Static query parameters. Values may be primitives.

body.description: Static JSON body for POST requests. Plain JSON — values may include {{var}} placeholders that the runtime interpolates as strings.

templates.description: Overrides / dynamic parts of the request. Each key is a dotted path that, when resolved against the request, replaces the static value at that location with the template value. Template values may be: a string with {{var}} placeholders (string interpolation), a number, a boolean, an array, or a nested object. They are NEVER stringified JSON that needs json.loads — they are direct JSON values.

at.description: Dotted path to the slot to override. Examples: 'headers.User-Agent', 'query.start', 'body.SearchParameters.FirstItem', 'body.SearchCriteria'. For 'url_path' paging.inject this is 'url'.

value.description: The template value. Any JSON-serialisable value. Strings may contain {{var}} placeholders.

variables.description: Defaults for {{var}} placeholders used in template values.

page_wrapper.description: JSON paths to extract the page-level counters and the list of items. All paths use dotted notation (e.g. 'data.positions') or JSON-pointer-style ('/data/positions').

locations.description: Declarative description of how to extract a list of human-readable location strings.

path.description: Dotted path to the raw locations value.

shape.description: If 'list_of_strings' the raw list is taken as-is. If 'list_of_objects' the runtime renders each item using 'item_template'.

item_template.description: Template for each object item. Placeholders are dotted paths RELATIVE to the item, e.g. '{DisplayName}' or '{CityName} ({CountryCode})'. Used only when shape=list_of_objects.

fallback_paths.description: Optional ordered list of dotted paths to try when the primary 'path' is missing or empty.

description.description: How to extract the full description text. May be sourced from the catalog item OR from a detail response (see detail.description_path).

path.description: Dotted path within the item to the description. If the value is a LIST of {Tasks, Qualifications} objects (e.g. Mercedes), use 'shape: list_of_blocks' to extract both halves.

shape.description: 'string' = the value at 'path' is the description. 'list_of_blocks' = the value at 'path' is a list of objects each with 'Tasks' and 'Qualifications' fields; the runtime joins them into description + qualifications using the optional relative keys.

tasks_relative_key.description: Relative key inside each block that holds the tasks text (used only when shape=list_of_blocks).

qualifications_relative_key.description: Relative key inside each block that holds the qualifications text (used only when shape=list_of_blocks).

join_separator.description: Separator used when shape=list_of_blocks joins multiple Tasks/Qualifications blocks.

strip_html.description: If true, the runtime strips HTML tags and collapses whitespace before storing.

fallback_paths.description: Optional ordered list of dotted paths to try when the primary 'path' is missing or empty (catalog or detail).

description_in_catalog.description: True if the catalog response already contains the full job description. If false, the runtime MUST issue a detail request per NEW or CHANGED item.

detail.description: Optional detail-request block. Required only when description_in_catalog is false.

templates.description: Same semantics as request.templates: dotted-path overrides with direct JSON values.

value.description: Any JSON-serialisable value. Strings may contain {{var}} placeholders.

interpolation.description: Where the stable_id is interpolated. 'query_param' (uses interpolation.name as key), 'body_path' (writes into body at the dotted path interpolation.name), 'url_path' (URL must contain {{stable_id}} placeholder).

name.description: Key name (query_param) or dotted body path (body_path) or '{{stable_id}}' marker (url_path).

strategy.description: v0.1 supports offset pagination only. page_number and cursor are not advertised in this version.

page_param.description: Query/body parameter name that carries the offset. For 'url_path' inject targets this is the {{page_param}} placeholder in the URL template.

first_page_value.description: Offset of the first page. Most sources start at 0 or 1.

inject.description: WHERE the runtime must put the offset value when building a request. Exhaustive — no inference.

target.description: Where the value is written. 'url_path' is intentionally excluded in v0.1 — we have no real source that needs it.

path.description: For 'body_path': dotted JSON path within the request body (e.g. 'SearchParameters.FirstItem'). For 'query_param': leave empty, the runtime uses paging.page_param.

default.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'EN') that the runtime injects into the request when the source expects one.

where.description: Where the language code goes in the request.

param.description: Parameter name. Defaults to 'language' / 'hl' / 'LanguageCode' depending on convention.

source_of_truth.description: Whether this source represents the COMPLETE company catalog (and is therefore authoritative for OPEN/CLOSED) or a FILTERED candidate view (which MUST NOT be used for CLOSED).

open_closed_authoritative.description: If true and source_of_truth == 'full_catalog', the runtime may use this source to compute authoritative CLOSED transitions (PIDs that disappeared from the full catalog are marked is_open=0).

completeness.description: Rigorously positive evidence that the catalog was traversed to the end.

rules.description: List of rules that must ALL hold true for catalog_complete = true. Each rule is a named check evaluated by the runtime.

config.description: Optional rule-specific config. For 'last_page_shorter_than_page_size': whether the protocol guarantees this (default true).

on_incomplete.description: What the runtime must do when ANY rule fails. 'skip_closed' (the safe default) means the source is treated as authoritative for the PIDs we DID see, but CLOSED transitions are NOT computed for missing PIDs.

sequential_only.description: Always true. No concurrency against this source.

min_seconds_between_requests.description: Minimum seconds between two requests. The runtime may add jitter on top.

max_requests_per_run.description: Hard ceiling on real HTTP attempts in a single run (including 5xx retries).

max_retries_on_5xx.description: Number of retries AFTER the original attempt. max_retries_on_5xx=1 means 1 original + 1 retry = 2 wire attempts.

not.description: Forbidden keys — if any of these appears, the spec is rejected.
